name: @superserve/mcp

tools.name: sandbox_create
tools.description: Create a new Superserve sandbox (a Firecracker microVM). Returns the sandbox id to use in subsequent tool calls. The sandbox is active and ready immediately.

from_template.description: Template (prebuilt base image) name or ID to base the sandbox on. Call sandbox_template_list first to see what your team has — don't guess a name.

from_snapshot.description: Snapshot ID to restore the sandbox from.

timeout_seconds.description: Idle timeout before the sandbox is auto-paused (max 604800 = 7 days).

auto_delete_seconds.description: Delete the sandbox once continuously paused for this many seconds (0 = delete on pause, max 2592000 = 30 days). Resume cancels the countdown. Omit to keep paused sandboxes forever.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key/value tags for filtering in sandbox_list.

env_vars.description: Plain environment variables for commands in the sandbox. Do NOT put credentials here — bind them with `secrets` instead so the real value never enters the sandbox.

secrets.description: Bind team-stored secrets to env vars: { ENV_VAR: secret_name }. The agent sees a proxy token; the platform swaps in the real credential at egress. List bindable secrets with secret_list. Create secrets via the Superserve SDK/console.

allow_out.description: Egress allow rules — domain patterns (e.g. 'api.github.com', '*.github.com'), IPs, or CIDRs to permit. This ADDS allowed destinations; on its own it does NOT block anything else. For a strict allowlist (deny everything except these), also pass deny_out: ['0.0.0.0/0']. If the allowlist has domain rules or the workload resolves hostnames, also include the sandbox DNS resolvers '1.1.1.1/32' and '8.8.8.8/32', or no hostname will resolve; leave them out of an IP-only allowlist.

deny_out.description: Egress deny rules — IPs or CIDRs, no domains (a bare IP is stored as its /32; use '0.0.0.0/0' to deny all egress). Combine deny_out: ['0.0.0.0/0'] with allow_out to lock the sandbox down to just the allowed destinations; deny-all also blocks DNS, so allow_out needs '1.1.1.1/32' and '8.8.8.8/32' whenever names must resolve.

preview_access.description: Default access for newly published ports. 'private' requires a per-port credential; 'public' requires publication but no credential (default).

tools.name: sandbox_template_list
tools.description: List the templates (prebuilt base images) your team can launch sandboxes from. Call this before sandbox_create to choose a from_template instead of guessing a name. Official templates are curated by Superserve, available to every team, and named with the reserved `superserve/` prefix — e.g. `superserve/python-3.11`, `superserve/node-22`, `superserve/openclaw`; names without that prefix are your team's own templates. Returns each template's name, status, and resources; only templates whose status is ready can be used.

name_prefix.description: Only return templates whose name starts with this prefix — e.g. 'superserve/' for the official curated templates, or 'python'.

tools.name: sandbox_template_create
tools.description: Build a reusable template (base image) so you can launch sandboxes with a specific vCPU/memory/disk shape or preinstalled software. Sandbox resources are inherited from the template and cannot be set at sandbox_create time, so this is how you get, say, a 4 vCPU sandbox. The build runs asynchronously: this returns immediately with status 'building' (or 'pending'). Poll sandbox_template_list (filter by name) until the template's status is 'ready' before passing it to sandbox_create's from_template. A build can take a few minutes.

name.description: Template name (your team's namespace; cannot start with the reserved 'superserve/').

from.description: Base image to build from, e.g. a Docker image like 'python:3.11' or 'ubuntu:24.04'.

vcpu.description: vCPU count for sandboxes built from this template.

memory_mib.description: Memory (MiB) for sandboxes built from this template.

disk_mib.description: Disk (MiB) for sandboxes built from this template.

run_steps.description: Shell commands run in order at build time, e.g. ['pip install numpy', 'apt-get install -y git']. Use these for env/workdir too (e.g. 'export X=Y && ...').

start_cmd.description: Command to start when a sandbox boots from this template.

ready_cmd.description: Command that must exit 0 before the build is considered ready.

tools.name: sandbox_list
tools.description: List your sandboxes (active and paused), optionally filtered by metadata. Returns ids, names, and statuses.

metadata.description: Filter to sandboxes whose metadata matches these key/values.

tools.name: sandbox_info
tools.description: Get current details (status, resources, metadata, timeout) for one sandbox by id. Read-only — does not resume a paused sandbox.

tools.name: sandbox_pause
tools.description: Pause a sandbox to save resources. State is preserved; resume it, or just run a command (exec auto-resumes).

sandbox_id.description: ID of the sandbox to pause.

tools.name: sandbox_resume
tools.description: Explicitly resume a paused sandbox. Usually unnecessary — sandbox_exec and the file tools auto-resume a paused sandbox.

sandbox_id.description: ID of the sandbox to resume.

tools.name: sandbox_kill
tools.description: Permanently delete a sandbox and all its state. Irreversible. Idempotent — deleting an already-deleted sandbox succeeds.

sandbox_id.description: ID of the sandbox to delete.

tools.name: sandbox_update
tools.description: Change a sandbox's metadata, egress network rules, auto-delete window, or auto-pause timeout after creation. Use this to lock down or open up outbound network access (rules apply to new connections), or to schedule cleanup of a sandbox you no longer need running. Only the fields you pass are changed.

sandbox_id.description: ID of the sandbox to update.

allow_out.description: Egress allow rules — domain patterns, IPs, or CIDRs to permit. Adds allowed destinations; does NOT by itself block other egress. For a strict allowlist, also pass deny_out: ['0.0.0.0/0']; if it has domain rules or the workload resolves hostnames, include the sandbox DNS resolvers '1.1.1.1/32' and '8.8.8.8/32'.

deny_out.description: Egress deny rules — IPs or CIDRs, no domains (a bare IP is stored as its /32; '0.0.0.0/0' denies all egress). Combine with allow_out to lock down egress; deny-all also blocks DNS, so allow_out needs '1.1.1.1/32' and '8.8.8.8/32' whenever names must resolve.

auto_delete_seconds.description: Delete the sandbox once continuously paused for this many seconds (max 2592000 = 30 days); the countdown starts now if it is already paused. Pass null to disable auto-delete. Omit to leave unchanged.

timeout_seconds.description: Idle timeout before the sandbox is auto-paused (max 604800 = 7 days). Pass null to disable auto-pause. Omit to leave unchanged.

preview_access.description: Change the default access for newly published ports. Existing ports keep their own mode.

tools.name: sandbox_preview_url
tools.description: Publish a sandbox port and return a browser-ready preview URL. Private ports receive an expiring signed URL; public ports receive a clean URL, and unpublished ports remain closed. This does not verify that a process is listening (start one with sandbox_exec, e.g. `python3 -m http.server 8000`).

port.description: The port a process is (or will be) listening on.

expires_in_seconds.description: Private signed-link lifetime in seconds (default 3600, max 604800 = 7 days). Ignored for public previews.

tools.name: sandbox_network_log
tools.description: List the outbound network connections a sandbox made (newest first) — host, verdict (allowed/blocked), bytes, and credential-injected requests. Use it to audit what a sandbox actually reached and to verify allow_out/deny_out rules. When has_more is true, pass next_cursor as before to fetch the next page. Read-only — does not resume a paused sandbox.

limit.description: Max rows to return (default 50, capped at 200).

before.description: Pagination cursor from the previous page's next_cursor, or an RFC3339 timestamp to return older events.

verdict.description: Filter to connections with this verdict.

tools.name: sandbox_exec
tools.description: Run a shell command in a Superserve sandbox and return stdout, stderr, and exit code. Paused sandboxes are resumed automatically — you do NOT need to resume first.

sandbox_id.description: ID of the sandbox to run in (from sandbox_create or sandbox_list).

command.description: Shell command to execute, e.g. "python script.py".

cwd.description: Working directory for the command (absolute path).

env.description: Extra environment variables for this command.

timeout_ms.description: Command timeout in milliseconds (default 60000, clamped to a max of 600000).

tools.name: sandbox_computer
tools.description: Drive a GUI desktop in a Superserve sandbox (requires a desktop template, e.g. superserve/desktop): capture screenshots and send mouse/keyboard input. One action per call. Input actions return a fresh screenshot of the result by default. Screen coordinates are [x, y] pixels with the origin at the top-left. Paused sandboxes are resumed automatically.

action.description: screenshot: capture the screen. left_click / right_click / middle_click / double_click / triple_click: click at `coordinate`. left_click_drag: drag from `start_coordinate` to `coordinate`. left_mouse_down / left_mouse_up: press/release at `coordinate`. mouse_move: move the pointer to `coordinate`. key: press a key or chord from `text` (e.g. 'Return', 'ctrl+s'). type: type the literal `text`. scroll: scroll `scroll_direction` by `scroll_amount` clicks (optionally at `coordinate`). wait: pause `duration_ms` for the UI to settle. resize: set the display to `width` x `height`. stream_url: get a live browser viewer URL for the desktop.

coordinate.description: [x, y] target pixel for pointer actions.

screenshot_after.description: Return a screenshot after input actions (default true). Set false when batching several actions back-to-back.

tools.name: sandbox_files_read
tools.description: Read a file from a sandbox. Returns UTF-8 text by default, or base64 when encoding is set to base64 (use it for binary files). Files larger than 1 MiB are rejected — read a slice with sandbox_exec instead.

path.description: Absolute path inside the sandbox, e.g. "/app/main.py".

tools.name: sandbox_files_write
tools.description: Write a file to a sandbox, creating or overwriting it. Parent directories are created automatically. Set encoding to base64 to write binary content. Inline content is limited to 8 MiB; upload larger files with the SDK/CLI.

path.description: Absolute path inside the sandbox, e.g. "/app/main.py".

content.description: File content (UTF-8 text, or base64 when encoding=base64).

tools.name: sandbox_files_list
tools.description: List directory contents in a sandbox. Returns name, type (file/directory/symlink), size, and modification time for each entry.

path.description: Absolute directory path to list, e.g. "/app".

tools.name: sandbox_files_download_dir
tools.description: Download a directory from a sandbox as a ZIP archive, returned base64-encoded in the result's structured content (symlinks are skipped). Use this to pull a whole folder — build output, results, a small project — in one call. Directories that zip to more than 10 MiB are rejected: grab a subdirectory, pull individual files with sandbox_files_read, or use the Superserve SDK/CLI for the full archive.

path.description: Absolute directory path to download, e.g. "/app/output".

tools.name: secret_list
tools.description: List the team's stored secrets you can bind to sandboxes — names, auth type, and allowed hosts. Returns metadata only; secret values never leave the platform. Bind one with sandbox_attach_secret or the secrets argument on sandbox_create. Create new secrets via the Superserve SDK or console.

tools.name: sandbox_attach_secret
tools.description: Bind a stored team secret to a sandbox under an environment variable. The sandbox sees a proxy token; the platform swaps in the real credential for outbound requests to the secret's allowed hosts. Takes effect for processes started after this call. Auto-resumes a paused sandbox.

env_key.description: Environment variable the sandbox reads, e.g. "OPENAI_API_KEY".

secret_name.description: Name of the stored secret to bind (see secret_list).

tools.name: sandbox_detach_secret
tools.description: Remove a secret binding from a sandbox by its environment-variable key. The proxy token is revoked, so requests using it are refused. Auto-resumes a paused sandbox. Idempotent.

env_key.description: Environment-variable key of the binding to remove.

instructions:
Superserve runs code in isolated Firecracker microVMs. Get a sandbox id first — call sandbox_create (or sandbox_list for existing ones), then pass sandbox_id to every other tool. sandbox_exec and the file tools auto-resume a paused sandbox, so never call sandbox_resume first. Use sandbox_pause to keep state cheaply; sandbox_kill deletes permanently. sandbox_files_read rejects files over 1 MiB — read a slice with sandbox_exec (e.g. `head -c`) instead of a full read.

Templates: call sandbox_template_list before passing from_template to sandbox_create; build a custom base image with sandbox_template_create, then poll sandbox_template_list until its status is ready. Secrets: bind stored credentials via the secrets argument on sandbox_create or sandbox_attach_secret instead of putting raw keys in env_vars; discover them with secret_list. Network: allow_out adds allowed destinations and deny_out blocks IPs or CIDRs (on sandbox_create or sandbox_update) — for a strict allowlist combine allow_out with deny_out:['0.0.0.0/0'], adding the DNS resolvers '1.1.1.1/32' and '8.8.8.8/32' when hostnames must resolve; audit HTTP/HTTPS egress with sandbox_network_log. Publish a listening port and get a browser-ready link with sandbox_preview_url; private ports receive an expiring signed URL.
